summary: Task 4 fully complies with Decision 6 (records + JsonNode stubs + @JsonIgnoreProperties), uses snake_case record components per existing project precedent (TelegramSendResult.error_code, TelegramUser.is_bot), and the package boundary com.botfunnel.webhook.dto cleanly resolves the name collision with com.botfunnel.user.User. Test suite covers all 9 task-listed cases plus slot independence, with appropriate exception class pinning (MismatchedInputException, JsonProcessingException). No critical or major findings.

suggestions.suggestion: Import order: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.exc.MismatchedInputException is imported before com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonProcessingException, which inverts Java's typical lexicographic order (core < databind). Cosmetic only; no functional impact and not enforced by a project linter that I can see.
suggestions.benefit: Consistency with idiomatic Java import grouping.

suggestions.suggestion: Chat record exposes only id/type/title/username, but private-chat updates also carry first_name/last_name. This is intentional per task scope (worker only consumes these four), and @JsonIgnoreProperties hides the rest — but a one-line javadoc note such as 'private-chat first_name/last_name are intentionally not modelled; added on demand by future epics' would prevent a future maintainer from concluding the record is incomplete.
suggestions.benefit: Reduces ambiguity for future contributors reading the DTO.

suggestions.suggestion: User record component naming uses snake_case (id, is_bot, first_name, ...). This is deliberate per Decision 6 (snake_case binding without @JsonProperty) and matches existing precedent (TelegramUser.is_bot). It is, however, the project's only DTO style that visibly diverges from Java naming conventions. Worth keeping a single ADR/decision pointer in a class-level javadoc on TelegramUpdate.java that links to Decision 6 — already done implicitly via the 'Jackson 2.12+ record support — no @JsonProperty required' line, so this is informational.
suggestions.benefit: Future readers immediately understand the snake_case choice was intentional.
